name: Lingtam
tagline: Warm river village just above Rongli
meta_description: Lingtam, Sikkim: the first village above Rongli on the Old Silk Route, about 1,500 m, with homestays, river walks and an easy start. Permit, costs and tips.
summary: Lingtam is the first village most travellers pass above Rongli on the Old Silk Route, at about 1,500 m, with cardamom, maize and vegetables around farmhouses. It is warm, quiet and low. Homestays here suit late arrivals and gentle starts. It lies inside the permit area, so a Rongli Silk Route permit is needed, for Indian nationals only.
intro: Lingtam lies along the Rongli river valley with forest on the slopes above and farm terraces below. It is roughly 8 km above Rongli and about 12 km below Padamchen, so it is the lowest and softest start to a Silk Route trip. Wikipedia names Dakline Lingtam among the hamlets of Pangolakha Wildlife Sanctuary, and Lingtam is one of the villages with a forest eco-development committee.

Because it is warmer than the places above, Lingtam suits travellers who arrive late in the day, who dislike cold nights or who want to sort paperwork at Rongli in the morning. Elevation figures vary between sources; around 1,400 to 1,600 m is a fair guide. Homestays are family-run and simple, usually with meals included.

Lingtam is inside the Silk Route protected area. The permit processed at Rongli is needed even to sleep here, and foreigners are not allowed. Check current status before you travel. From Lingtam, Padamchen is about 12 km and Zuluk about 25 km up the road.

story.title: The first stage above Rongli
story.text: Rongli, Wikipedia says, is one of the oldest markets of Sikkim, on the trade route between Kalimpong and Tibet. The Jelep La article describes the Kalimpong route as passing through Rongli, Rhenock and Pedong, and says wool and furs were traded along it in the twentieth century. Lingtam is the first village on the climb after Rongli, which makes it a natural stopping point for walkers and muleteers who started late. The Dzuluk article records that traders used Zuluk as an overnight base on the route running through Pedong, Aritar, Zuluk and Jelep La into the Chumbi valley until about 1959. Today the road carries tourist jeeps and army trucks instead of mules. Wikipedia names Dakline Lingtam in the list of hamlets of Pangolakha Wildlife Sanctuary, and says an eco-development committee works in Lingtam to protect the forest. The old trade traffic has gone, but the village still sits where the route starts to climb.
story.source: Wikipedia: Rongli; Wikipedia: Jelep La; Wikipedia: Dzuluk; Wikipedia: Pangolakha Wildlife Sanctuary

little_known.fact: Wikipedia names Dakline Lingtam among the hamlets of Pangolakha Wildlife Sanctuary and lists Lingtam among villages with forest eco-development committees.
Wikipedia lists Lingtam among the villages around Rongli town, alongside Padamchen, Zuluk, Rolep, Kupup and Gnathang, which shows how much of the Silk Route falls in Rongli subdivision.
Rongli sits on National Highway 717B, which Wikipedia says runs from Rhenock to Menla near Sherathang via Zuluk, so the road you take through Lingtam has a highway number.

facts: Mar–May and Oct–Dec; warm in winter
Farmstay, river views, gentle first night
Silk Route permit via Rongli, Indian nationals only

highlights.title: Warm start to the Silk Route
highlights.text: Lingtam's lower height keeps nights mild, so it suits families, seniors and anyone who feels the cold. You can climb to Padamchen and Zuluk the next day.

highlights.title: Farm and cardamom lanes
highlights.text: Walks around the village pass cardamom, maize, ginger and vegetables near farmhouses. Ask your host before entering fields and for the safest lanes.

highlights.title: River sounds and short walks
highlights.text: The Rongli river runs nearby and gives a soft background all evening. Stay out of the main channel and never swim after rain upstream.

highlights.title: Late-arrival stop
highlights.text: If the Rongli permit office closes before you finish, Lingtam is the nearest sensible place to sleep. Arrange the permit with your homestay in advance where possible.

highlights.title: Forest edge birds
highlights.text: Early morning walks near the tree line can show laughingthrushes, bulbuls and sunbirds. We do not promise particular species.

how_to_reach.text: Take a shared jeep from Gangtok or Siliguri to Rongli, about ₹200–400 a seat, finish the permit there and then use a local permit-registered vehicle for the roughly 8 km to Lingtam. Local fares are small, but there are few shared services after midday.

From Gangtok about 75 km and 3.5 hours via Pakyong, Rorathang and Rongli. A reserved small car costs around ₹4,500–6,000 for a Silk Route day, more for an SUV. Check current status of roads before you travel.

About 120 km and 5 hours via Sevoke, Rangpo and Rorathang. NH10 can close after monsoon slides; the alternative is via Kalimpong and Pedong. Pakyong Airport has no scheduled flights, so plan on Bagdogra (IXB) or NJP.

where_to_stay: Lingtam has farmhouse homestays at about ₹1,200–1,700 per person with meals; our lingtam-homestays listing describes them. They are the lowest, warmest beds on the Silk Route, so they suit winter nights and small children. For more height, sleep at Padamchen or Zuluk; for more comfort, Aritar or Pakyong have better options. Ask the host to arrange the permit before you arrive. We do not name families, so ask us for current availability.
tips: Treat Lingtam as the low night: it is the best choice if you feel the cold or arrive late.
Carry ID for every traveller, and two passport photos, for the Rongli permit.
The permit is needed even to stay in Lingtam, so do not skip Rongli.
Avoid river edges after rain; levels rise quickly.
Check current status of NH10 and the Rongli road before you leave.

experiences.title: Cardamom and kitchen garden walk
experiences.summary: A slow walk through Lingtam's terraces where cardamom grows under shade beside maize, ginger and vegetables, with a host who explains each crop.
body: Large cardamom is a key cash crop of Sikkim and the farms around Lingtam grow it under alder trees. The capsules are picked in autumn and dried before sale. Wikipedia describes the plant and its uses in cooking.

Walk with your host or a guide along farm lanes. Ask before entering fields, photographing families or picking anything. Most families are happy to explain how they work if you show interest and respect.
The walk is gentle but steps can be slippery after rain. Wear shoes with grip, carry water and take your litter back. If you want to buy a small packet of cardamom, ask for the day's price.

faqs.q: When is cardamom harvested?
faqs.a: Usually in autumn, around September to November, followed by drying. Visits in spring show the plants in green leaf. Dates vary, so ask your host. We cannot promise to show drying in progress.

faqs.q: Can children join the walk?
faqs.a: Yes. The paths are mostly gentle, but steps can be slippery. Keep children close, avoid wet days and carry water. A short walk of one hour suits young children.

faqs.q: Can we buy cardamom?
faqs.a: Yes, in small packets, at a price that changes with the market. Check that pods are dry and fragrant. Keep them sealed. Ask your host for the current rate and do not expect bargains.

experiences.title: Rongli river edge walk
experiences.summary: A short, careful walk to the river near Lingtam to listen, watch birds and see the water that later joins the Rangpo river.
body: Wikipedia says Rongli Khola and the Rangpo river meet at Rongli, and the Rangpo then flows past Rorathang to join the Teesta at Rangpo town. The stream near Lingtam is part of this river system.
Walk with your host or guide to a safe bank. In winter the river is shallow, and in monsoon it rises fast. Never swim in the main channel. Keep children away from the edge and do not cross wet rocks.
Birds such as brown dippers can be seen on fast streams in the sanctuary region, though we cannot promise sightings. Go early or at dusk, move quietly and take your litter with you.

faqs.q: Is the river safe for swimming?
faqs.a: No. Currents can be strong and water can rise suddenly after upstream rain, especially from June to September. Paddling in a shallow edge pool in winter can be fine, with a local's advice. Never swim in the main channel.

faqs.q: When is the best time to walk to the river?
faqs.a: Between October and April in settled weather, when water is low and paths dry. Avoid the monsoon and the day after heavy rain. Early morning is quietest.

faqs.q: Do we need a guide for the river walk?
faqs.a: Not strictly, but a host or local guide knows which banks are safe and which paths have slipped. It costs little or nothing at a homestay. Ask before you set off.

experiences.title: Farmhouse supper and evening chat
experiences.summary: Dinner in a Lingtam farmhouse, with produce from the garden, tea afterwards and unhurried conversation about the road and the seasons.
body: Lingtam homestays are working farms, so meals often use what is growing nearby: greens, squash, beans, maize and ginger. Rice and dal are constants, with a meat or egg dish for those who want one.
Ask about gundruk and pickles. Fermented foods are part of local kitchens, and your host may offer a taste. Say if you have allergies or dietary needs when you book.
Evenings are mild compared with Padamchen. Sit and listen if invited, and ask questions with respect. Avoid asking people to pose or perform. Bring a torch because electricity can fail.

faqs.q: Is the food spicy?
faqs.a: Home cooking is usually mild to medium, with dalle chilli pickle on the side if you want heat. Ask for less chilli when booking. Children are usually catered for.

faqs.q: Can vegetarians eat well?
faqs.a: Yes. Rice, dal, vegetables and greens are the base of most meals. Say if you avoid onion, garlic or eggs. Allow notice for special diets.

faqs.q: Do homestays take UPI or cards?
faqs.a: Often not reliably. Network signal can fail. Carry cash. The nearest ATMs are at Rongli and Rhenock.

experiences.title: Permit morning and Rongli bazaar stop
experiences.summary: A relaxed start at Rongli: finish your Silk Route permit with a host or agent, then walk the bazaar, the oldest market on this trade road.
body: Rongli is where the Silk Route permit is processed, usually in 30 to 60 minutes. Your driver or homestay takes documents into the office. Keep original ID, photocopies and two passport photos ready.

While you wait, walk the bazaar. Wikipedia calls Rongli one of the oldest markets of Sikkim, on the trade route between Kalimpong and Tibet. You will find tea shops, groceries, banks, ATMs and shared jeep stands.
Buy snacks, water and any medicines before going up, because supplies are limited above. Offices keep government hours and may close on holidays. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How long does the permit take?
faqs.a: Often 30 to 60 minutes if documents are complete, longer on busy weekends. Offices keep government hours and may close on holidays. Arrange it through your homestay in advance if possible. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What documents do we need?
faqs.a: Original photo ID for every traveller, photocopies and two passport photos each, children included. The permit is in your name for dates and a vehicle. Indian nationals only. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Where can we withdraw cash?
faqs.a: Rongli and Rhenock have ATMs, but they can be empty or offline. Withdraw cash in Gangtok, Pakyong or Rangpo before you head up. Carry small notes for homestays.

faqs.q: What is Lingtam?
faqs.a: Lingtam is a village at about 1,500 m, the first on the Old Silk Route after Rongli. It has farmhouse homestays, cardamom and vegetable farms and a mild climate. It lies inside the permit area and is often used as a warm first night.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to stay in Lingtam?
faqs.a: Yes. Lingtam is inside the Silk Route protected area, so the Rongli permit is needed even to sleep there. Indian nationals only. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: How far is Lingtam from Rongli?
faqs.a: About 8 km, taking 20 to 30 minutes on a winding road. Landslides can add delays. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is Lingtam warmer than Zuluk?
faqs.a: Yes, much. Lingtam at about 1,500 m is mild even in winter, while Zuluk at about 2,800 m has frost and occasional snow. Bring warmer layers for the upper villages.

faqs.q: Is Lingtam a good first night for the Silk Route?
faqs.a: Yes, especially for late arrivals, families with young children and anyone who feels the cold. Padamchen is the next step up in height. Many travellers combine Lingtam, Padamchen and Zuluk across three nights.

faqs.q: Can foreigners visit Lingtam?
faqs.a: No, because Lingtam is inside the protected area, and the Old Silk Route is for Indian nationals only. Foreign visitors can stay at Aritar or Rhenock instead. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: What is there to do in Lingtam?
faqs.a: Farm walks, river-edge strolls, birdwatching at the forest edge and home-cooked meals. There are no major sights. It is a quiet village for slowing down.

faqs.q: How much does a Lingtam homestay cost?
faqs.a: About ₹1,200–1,700 per person a night with meals, indicative. Confirm what is included. Cash is needed. Check current status before you travel.

faqs.q: Is there mobile signal in Lingtam?
faqs.a: Signal is patchy and can drop in rain or in valley bottoms. Do not rely on UPI or maps. Download maps in advance and carry cash.
